cards.explanation: The answer is to oversee the work of the LORD's house. David says, "24,000 are to oversee the work of the house of the LORD…" (1 Chronicles 23:4). That's more than half of the 38,000 Levites. Somebody has to keep the whole operation running, friends, and it takes a crowd.

The answer is to praise the LORD with instruments. David says 4,000 "…are to praise the LORD with the instruments I have made for giving praise." (1 Chronicles 23:5). That's a whole band, friends. I'd love to hear that rehearsal.

The answer is David. He's the one talking in verse 5, and he says the instruments are ones "…I have made for giving praise." (1 Chronicles 23:5). The man didn't just order a band, friends, he built the instruments for it. I can't even get my mustache to hold a tambourine and a spatula at once, so I'm impressed.

The word is carry. David says, "So now the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the articles for its service." (1 Chronicles 23:26). The reason he gives is that the LORD "…has come to dwell in Jerusalem forever." (1 Chronicles 23:25). I think those Levites were happy to put down the heavy stuff.

The answer is the descendants of Aaron. The Levites' duty was "…to assist the descendants of Aaron with the service of the house of the LORD…" (1 Chronicles 23:28). Aaron's family was set apart for the most holy things (1 Chronicles 23:13). So the Levites were the helpers, friends, and every good kitchen has them.

The answer is False. The Levites were to be "…responsible for the courts and chambers, the purification of all the holy things, and the work of the service of the house of God…" (1 Chronicles 23:28). They're in charge of those places, not kept out of them. Think of it as having the keys, friends.

The answer is the baking and the mixing. The list includes "…the baking, the mixing, and all measurements of quantity and size." (1 Chronicles 23:29). Measuring is on there too. Baking, mixing and measuring all on one job list, bakers, and I'm a little jealous.

The answer is every morning and every evening. The Levites "…were also to stand every morning to give thanks and praise to the LORD, and likewise in the evening." (1 Chronicles 23:30). Twice a day, every day, friends. That's a steady habit of thanks.

The answer is True. The verse says, "So the Levites were to carry out the responsibilities for the Tent of Meeting and the Holy Place…" (1 Chronicles 23:32). They also served the house of the LORD under their brothers, the descendants of Aaron. That's a good wrap-up for a long list, bakers.
